A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original Bayesian-regression simulations and GSM8K experiments using Llama-3-8B-Instruct with a Mistral judge, including additional simulations in Appendix G.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulations and LLM experiments and adds results for further base models and a process reward judge in Figure 12 and Appendix G.2.

M1.justification: The proposed Bayesian regression model, quadratic theoretical reward and reward-weighted sampling algorithm are unchanged. Appendix F's speculative extensions are also retained. Additional LLMs and the PRM serve as experimental configurations of the existing framework.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic Gaussian linear regression and GSM8K mathematical reasoning. The additional base models and judges do not introduce another dataset, population or task requirement.

E2.justification: v2 adds Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-7B as an evaluated judging alternative to Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3. Appendix G.2 contrasts their behavior using shared Llama and Gemma base models. The original weak-versus-strong Mistral prompt comparison remains.

E3.justification: Added experiments expand evaluation from one base LLM to six and introduce PRM-based best-of-k and reward-temperature configurations. Existing synthetic settings also change: Figure 4 adds c=85, and Figure 5 replaces c=40,50 with c=75,80,85,90. Newly disclosed generation settings are not evidence that retained experiments changed.

E4.justification: Figure 12 adds empirical best-of-k scaling fits, while Figures 17–24 test temperature sensitivity and sampling behavior across additional base models and causal versus process judges. Figures 4–5 revise existing reward-misspecification sensitivity analyses. The original appendix parameter sweeps remain as Figures 13–16.

E5.justification: Figure 12 introduces empirical power-law fitting with estimated prefactors and exponents. Existing mean-plus/minus-one-standard-deviation displays remain; v2 provides no new repeated-run counts, seeds or uncertainty estimates for the fitted parameters.

E6.justification: New Figure 12 reports error fits of 0.463/k^0.063 for DeepSeek and 0.219/k^0.187 for Llama, alongside additional model/judge results in Appendix G.2. Existing numerical results also change: Figure 4's reported k_opt at c=78 changes from 44 to 34. Figure 5 supplies replacement results under different reward settings, not a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: Appendix A removes the explicit continuity-point qualifications from Result 4 and Definition 5, making those formal statements less explicit. The principal deterministic-equivalent results, temperature expansions, k^-2 law and supporting proof arguments remain; extensive equation reformatting does not constitute new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract and central analytical claims are retained. The introduction adds an empirical contribution claiming analogous best-of-k power-law behavior with a nearly ideal PRM judge and broadens the claimed LLM validation beyond the original Llama/Mistral setup.

C2.justification: Section 4 newly interprets the PRM as a nearly ideal reward and connects its empirical scaling curves to the theoretical result, while acknowledging different exponents. It also distinguishes reasoning-aware judge selection from pass@k. Existing future-work qualifications are largely relocated.

D1.justification: New Appendix G.2 documents the evaluation-harness task, vLLM backend, generation temperature 0.2, answer formatting and extraction, and explicit weak/strong judge prompts. It also describes PRM step segmentation, separator tokens and score scaling. v1 largely referred readers to code for prompt details; the repository link itself is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 shifts its closest-prior-work discussion from Levi's model to Brown and Schaeffer's scaling laws. Section 4 adds a distinction from their pass@k analyses. These are limited positioning changes involving works already cited in v1.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain. There are localized introduction and conclusion edits, movement of future-work discussion into the conclusion, and subdivision of Appendix G into synthetic-model results and LLM experimental details.

P2.justification: Panels from v1 Figures 6–8 become larger standalone Figures 6–11; Figures 4–5 are redrawn with revised legends and ranges. v2 adds Figure 12, Figures 17–24 and prompt-example boxes, relocates retained appendix plots, and extensively reformats displayed equations.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens v1's narrow empirical validation by testing multiple base models and contrasting causal and process judges, including the strong-reward best-of-k regime. Appendix G.2 also supplies previously missing protocol and prompt details, materially improving reproducibility. These gains outweigh the limited loss of explicit formal qualifications, although the empirical fits support a qualitative analogy rather than confirming the theoretical k^-2 exponent.
